keyframe_review.note: 26,770 km2 (110 cells): Kraków, Tarnów, Nowy Sącz, Oświęcim and the Tatra foothills (the bbox reaches 49.2 N, into today's Slovakia). 'the duchies of Kraków and Sandomierz were inherited by Leszek II' on Bolesław the Chaste's death on 7 December 1279; Cliopatria draws Kraków separately and Sandomierz as its own shape. No page opened gives the duchy's area or borders.

26,864 km2 (112 cells): two more cells than 1279, taken from the Opole shape; no page opened explains it (Bytom and Racibórz are carved from Opole in 1285). The Leszek page has the third Mongol invasion of Lesser Poland of 1287-1288 and Leszek's death on 30 September 1288 without a border change.

region.text: the Kraków lands: Kraków, Tarnów, Nowy Sącz, Oświęcim and the Tatra foothills

ledger.note: 7 December 1279: Bolesław the Chaste dies and Leszek the Black inherits Kraków. 'On 7 December 1279, Bolesław the Chaste died'; 'the duchies of Kraków and Sandomierz were inherited by Leszek II'. The Duchy of Kraków page says the duchy was formed in 1227; Cliopatria draws it as a separate polity from 1279.

1290: Przemysł II of Greater Poland becomes Duke of Kraków. The ruler list: Leszek II 1279-1288, Bolesław II of Masovia 1288 and 1289, Henry IV Probus 1288-1289 and 1289-1290, Władysław I 1289, Przemysł II 1290-1291; the Leszek page says Probus 'became high duke in 1289' and 'died a year later, and the Seniorate passed to Przemysł II'. The land does not change hands in Cliopatria.
1291: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia takes Kraków. The ruler list gives Wenceslaus II 1291-1300 and the infobox 'fiefdom status, 1300'. Cliopatria draws the Kraków lands with Bohemia only from 1294.

region.text: the whole duchy of Cliopatria's last shape

ledger.note: 1293: the last year of Cliopatria's Kraków shape. The Duchy of Kraków page has the duchy independent until 1300, 'a fiefdom within the Kingdom of Poland' 1300-1320 and incorporated into the Crown lands in 1320; Wenceslaus II of Bohemia is duke 1291-1300. Cliopatria's Bohemia shape covers the land from 1294; the year is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Leo I of Galicia's invasion of Lublin and the Battle of Goźlice
wars.outcome: In February 1280 Leo, backed by Wenceslaus II of Bohemia and others, invaded Lublin and besieged Sandomierz; Polish forces drove him off at Goźlice on 23 February 1280. The fighting was in Sandomierz and Lublin lands, outside the Kraków shape.

wars.name: Yotvingian and Lithuanian raids on Lublin
wars.outcome: The Yotvingians invaded Lublin in 1282 and Leszek defeated them; a Lithuanian retaliatory raid was beaten at Rowiny in 1283.

wars.name: Rebellion of 1285 and the Battle of Bogucice
belligerents: Rebels of Otto Toporczyk, Janusz Starża and Żegota
wars.outcome: Rebels forced Leszek to flee to Hungary in April 1285; with Hungarian help he won at Bogucice on 3 May 1285. Konrad II of Czersk, the rebels' candidate, failed to take Wawel Castle.

wars.name: Third Mongol invasion of Lesser Poland
wars.outcome: Nogai Khan and Talabuga invaded while Leszek sought help in Hungary; the page records no border change.

wars.name: Dispute for the Seniorate Province after Leszek the Black
wars.outcome: 'After his death, a violent dispute erupted among the main Piast rulers for the Seniorate Province': Bolesław II of Masovia, Henry IV Probus (high duke in 1289, died a year later), Przemysł II (1290-1291), then Wenceslaus II of Bohemia (1291-1300).
wars.note: The Duchy of Kraków page lists the dukes; the Silesia dossier records Probus taking Kraków in August 1289.

certainty.note: The pages give no borders; the shape is Cliopatria's.

notes: Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for this row ('Grand Duchy of Kraków', Q688918) is the Habsburg Grand Duchy of 1846-1918, which has nothing on the medieval duchy; the correct article is 'Duchy of Kraków' (formed 1227, independent to 1300, fief of the Kingdom of Poland 1300-1320), used here. Cliopatria draws Kraków inside its Sandomierz outline until 1279 (110 of 110 cells); this dossier starts the state at 1279, as the Sandomierz dossier records the split, although the Duchy page dates the duchy to 1227: Kraków before 1279 is drawn as Sandomierz. The ruler list overlaps in 1288-1290 (Bolesław II of Masovia, Henry IV Probus, Władysław I, all 'duke of Kraków'): the map shows one Kraków. Wenceslaus II is duke from 1291 on the page but Cliopatria draws Bohemia over the land only from 1294. The shape reaches 49.2 N, into Slovakia, which no page confirms. The page budget was one or two pages; three were opened because the first was the wrong article. Gazetteer: no new names.
